title: The 5 Biggest Impact Craters on Earth, Ranked (Dino Killer Is Only #2)

scenes.text: The five biggest asteroid scars on Earth. The one that killed the dinosaurs isn't number one.

scenes.label: Acraman · about 90 km
scenes.text: Number five: Acraman, in South Australia. About 90 kilometers wide, and nearly 600 million years old.

scenes.label: Popigai · about 90 km
scenes.text: Number four: Popigai, in Siberia. Also about 90 kilometers, and the impact left the rock full of diamonds.

scenes.label: Sudbury · 130 km
scenes.text: Number three: Sudbury, in Canada. 130 kilometers across, and today one of the world's great nickel mining regions.

scenes.label: Chicxulub · 150 km
scenes.text: Number two: Chicxulub, in Mexico. 150 kilometers, buried under the Yucatan, and the end of the dinosaurs.

scenes.label: Vredefort · 160 km
scenes.text: Number one: Vredefort, in South Africa. 160 kilometers across today, two billion years old, and it may once have been 300.

description:
The five biggest confirmed impact craters on Earth, ranked by the diameter listed in the Earth Impact Database.
Vredefort in South Africa is the largest and, at about 2.02 billion years, one of the oldest; erosion has removed much of it, and estimates of its original size run to 250 or 300 km. Chicxulub in Mexico (150 km in the database, about 180 km in other estimates) is the crater of the impact that ended the age of the dinosaurs 66 million years ago. Sudbury in Canada (130 km, 1.85 billion years) is a major nickel mining district. Popigai in Siberia and Acraman in South Australia are both listed at 90 km; Popigai, 35.7 million years old, is known for its impact diamonds. Manicouagan in Quebec, at 85 km, just misses the list.
Which one would you most like to stand in?
first_comment: Manicouagan in Quebec just misses at 85 km, and its ring-shaped lake is nicknamed the Eye of Quebec. Which crater would you put at #1, and what should we rank next?
